concepts.def: Community of French-speaking countries; the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie has 88 member states.
North-west Africa: Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia — colonised by France and a major source of post-war immigration.
Includes Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Mali, Cameroon — official French alongside national languages.
French-speaking province of Canada; Law 101 (1977) made French the sole official language.
French colonial empire reached its peak in the early 20th century; decolonisation accelerated 1956–62.
Creole languages spoken in Haiti, Martinique, Guadeloupe, Réunion — French-based but distinct.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Topic 4: The World Around Us — a core area of GCSE French.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Topic 4: The World Around Us brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Topic 4: The World Around Us.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In which year did Algeria gain independence from France?
Which is NOT part of the Maghreb?

numericals.q: In what year was Quebec's Law 101 (Charter of the French Language) passed?

free_texts.q: What is the French word for 'colonisation'?
